checks.title: Every Request Time Off definition has the form steps
checks.why: A tenant can run several definitions of one process (by organization). Each one that should carry a form needs FormAssign and FormGate Service steps.

checks.title: Every Change Job definition has the form steps
checks.why: Same as above. The dev tenant has Change Job (Default Definition) and Change Job (Simplified for Data Entry).

checks.title: Every Onboarding definition has the form steps
checks.why: Launch Onboarding used the org-specific definition (Onboarding for Next Level Enterprise), not the default one.

checks.title: Route records readable (TEST:DYN:ROUTE)
checks.query: SELECT responseKey, status FROM developertoolkitappv1_kwswrv_dynResponses WHERE responseKey startswith "TEST:DYN:ROUTE"
checks.why: HR routing needs both the event's [ROUTE:HR] comment and the worker's route record written by FormGate.

checks.title: Calculated fields and condition rule for routing
checks.text: Present and in use: TEST DYN Comment Route HR (Comment contains [ROUTE:HR]), TEST DYN Event Route HR Comments (Action Event, count), TEST DYN Route HR Flag (DynResponse), TEST DYN Route HR Count (Worker), TEST DYN LRV Event Route HR Count (Action Event, LRV via Worker). Condition rule TEST DYN Route HR = Event Route HR Comments > 0 And LRV Event Route HR Count > 0. Rule Usage should list every definition's routed step.
checks.why: Calculated fields and condition rules are tenant configuration: they don't travel with the app.

checks.title: Each definition: steps, Run As and inputs
checks.text: On every definition found above: Service FormAssign (actionEvent = Workday ID, formCode, worker = WID from Field Worker), Run As the forms ISU; Service FormGate after the last step the requester completes, Run As the forms ISU; a Route marker To Do next to it; the routed step's condition = TEST DYN Route HR. Sub-processes that route need their own gate and marker.
checks.why: WQL shows step types, not which orchestration a Service step runs.

checks.title: FormEnded on Cancel, Rescind and Deny (Configure Orchestrations)
checks.text: Per definition: rows for Cancel, Rescind and Deny where offered, each with a launch configuration for its process type (FormEnded, actionEvent = Determine WID at Runtime, Business Process Event) and User to Perform Orchestration Launches = the forms ISU. Tenant setting Edit Tenant Setup - Business Processes > User to perform Orchestration Launches must be set first.
checks.why: Without it a cancelled request's forms stay in My Forms until the hourly FormReconcile run.

checks.title: Grants for the forms ISU's security group
checks.text: On each process policy: View All and Cancel (Web Service). On the app domain Use: Developer Toolkit: Report/Task View and Modify, Integration Get and Put. On Dyn Confidential Answers: Integration Get and Put (HR Administrator: View). The Person-field grant that lets FormAssign read the event's Person (bpPerson). Then Activate Pending Security Policy Changes.
checks.why: A missing grant doesn't stop the step: the orchestration fails quietly and the step still advances. Check each run's Orchestrations tab.

checks.title: Confidential answers hidden from non-HR users
checks.text: As a user with the app's domain but not Dyn Confidential Answers (dev: Teresa Serrano via TEST:DYN Non-HR App Viewer): Results shows the confidential column blank, and WQL on dynAnswers leaves secretText out.
checks.why: The field-level domain is the control a buyer's security team will ask about.
